title: Tenant-aware LSH-based coalescing and adaptive invalidation for embedding cache
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Problem: Our embedding endpoint sees significant redundant work when multiple requests contain semantically similar or identical texts. Existing exact-key prefix caching reduces some duplicates but fails for paraphrases and small edits, and TTL-only policies cause stale cache entries after model updates or quality regressions. We need a solution that increases effective cache hit rate without risking cross-tenant leakage or unacceptable quality regressions for reranking customers.

Proposal: Implement a tenant-aware approximate coalescing layer using locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) + HMAC tenant scoping, combined with adaptive invalidation signals. Key ideas: 1) generate compact LSH fingerprints for inputs at the request edge and use them to route to a per-tenant coalescer that can answer: is there a recent embedding close enough to reuse? 2) Use tenant-specific HMAC seeds to ensure no cross-tenant key reuse and to enable per-tenant opt-out. 3) Maintain a two-tier cache: a small hot in-memory L1 (GPU-local or node-local) with strict eviction and a larger L2 persistent store (shared Redis/Memcached) storing canonical embeddings and metadata (model version, quality score). 4) Adaptive invalidation: tie cache TTLs and eviction aggressiveness to model-version rollouts, quality regression signals from Evaluate (prompt sets), and explicit tenant policy. 5) Safety: when LSH indicates a match but distance is near threshold, fall back to on-the-fly embedding computation and optionally store both; track false-positive rate and user-visible quality delta.

Implementation plan: Phase 1 (prototype): LSH encoder library in Rust (same infra as runtime kernels) + small in-memory index with sample collisions guard. Build a lightweight coalescer sidecar that exposes a sync API for edge nodes. Phase 2: integrate tenant HMAC keys, L2 persistence API, and instrument end-to-end telemetry. Phase 3: A/B rollout for a subset of non-enterprise customers and then to Dedicated after SLA verification.

Metrics/acceptance criteria: - Effective cache hit rate >= 30% on high-duplicate workloads. - End-to-end embedding request p95 reduced by >= 20% on observed workloads that dedupe. - False-positive-induced quality regression on reranking AUC <= 1.0% absolute. - No cross-tenant key leakage verified by security review and unit tests.

Benchmarks & targets: our small-scale prototype (see updates) showed a 38% effective hit rate on a sample of query logs and reduced end-to-end p95 from 420ms to 310ms for embedding requests on the test cluster. We observed a 2.1% LSH false-positive rate that translated into a -0.8% AUC delta on a narrow rerank test set; this is within tolerances but requires monitoring and conservative thresholds for production rollouts.

Rollout & risk mitigation: start with low-risk cohorts (non-SLA, small tenants) and require a manual opt-in for enterprise tenants. Instrument quality telemetry (A/B per-tenant) and provide immediate rollback when model-update signals indicate regression. Use HMAC scoping and tenant keys to satisfy compliance and audit requirements.

Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EMB/LSH+Embed+Coalescer. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821. Benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embeddings/lsh-proto-v1.
updates: 2026-03-05 - Triaged by Embeddings infra squad. Assigned to Diego. Core idea: approximate matching with tenant HMAC to avoid cross-tenant dedupe.

2026-03-07 - Spike: implemented Rust LSH encoder and micro-benchmarked fingerprinting cost (~0.6ms per 512-token input on c5-like CPUs). Decision: use 128-bit SimHash variant for speed and small footprint.

2026-03-09 - Prototype: built sidecar coalescer and integrated with edge request flow in staging. Observed effective hit-rate 38% on sampled query logs (non-uniform distribution). End-to-end embedding p95 improved from 420ms -> 310ms in our staging cluster. See prototype PR for code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821.

2026-03-10 - Design review notes from PM (Maya Chen) and Security (Omar Patel): require tenant-scoped HMAC keys for index entries, and encrypted storage for L2. Also: must expose opt-out flag per tenant. Action: add HMAC key rotation and per-tenant policy flags.

2026-03-11 - QA: ran rerank quality smoke tests. LSH false-positive rate ~2.1% resulted in AUC delta -0.8% on narrow rerank set. Follow-up: tune similarity threshold and add 'conservative mode' for rerank endpoints that prefer compute over reuse when close to threshold.

2026-03-13 - Engineering decision: adopt two-threshold policy (reuse if distance < T1; if T1 <= distance < T2 then compute-and-compare; if >= T2 compute-only). This reduces measurable quality regressions at cost of fewer reuses. Updated implementation plan and estimate.
Next steps: finalize HMAC rotation PR, add per-tenant policy flags in console, run a 2-week A/B test on 10% traffic for non-enterprise tenants, and prepare security review packet.
